messages:
devon: Heads-up — spotted ~12 pods in ap-southeast1 that are Pending but tied to tiny-gpu requests (0.125 GPU). Nodes report 1 GPU used but <10% utilization overall. Looks like a consolidation opportunity.
ashley: Oh nice catch. Are they spread across racks or concentrated?
kai: Quick note: we've had egress policer spikes in that region earlier today, some racks went into soft-throttle for ~6m. Could explain delayed scheduling/latebind.
devon: They're mostly on 3 racks. Logs show containers in those tiny pods keep flapping init containers and holding the GPU slot. snippet:
```
Name             Status    Node              GPU
job-lite-42      Pending   —                 0.125
pod-alpha        Running   gpu-nodex-3rack2 1.000 (occupied by tiny sidecar)
```
liam: If sidecars are occupying the device long after main task exits, that's our classic shelf-adhesion. We should consider a reclaim on those low-priority tiny pods.
sara: Reclaim + binpack script? We can drain the 3 racks to a consolidation pool and move long-lived tiny workloads to vCPU-only instances.
devon: Cost-wise, moving small workloads off GPUs could save ~12% on token-inference cost (rough estimate from last week's telemetry). But we need a safe rollout.
ashley: Suggestion: run a conservative canary that evicts pods with priority <= P10 and age > 30m, and only if node GPU utilization < 20%. Add a cooldown so we don't thrash.
kai: Also watch egress bandwidth — when we reschedule, pods will pull models (30–200MB) which can bump egress and trigger policer again. Can we throttle model fetch concurrency?
liam: Yes, we can gate re-schedules with a token bucket. I'll add a limiter to the reclaim job: max-ttl-fetch-concurrency=3. Also set nodeDrainGrace=90s.
infra-bot: ALERT: ap-southeast1 rack-b7 experienced egress-police event at 2026-03-20T13:42:11Z — avg NIC utilization 96% for 6m
sara: Good call @liam. Also add node annotation so we don't blast a single AZ's cache miss at once: annotate with "reclaim-group" and rotate targets.
devon: Plan: 1) run dry-run reclaim to generate move list; 2) canary drain 1 node per rack with limiter; 3) measure model fetch egress and latency; 4) rollback if any p95 latency regresses >30%.
ashley: Who wants to own canary run? I can spin it up after lunch and monitor.
kai: I'll keep an eye on egress policer metrics and add temporary routing to eu fallback if policer trips.
liam: I'll prepare the script. Dry-run output will be in S3: s3://redwood-infra/reclaims/1772000123/dry-run.json
sara: Add a post-mortem checklist entry: confirm no job priority inversion, verify warm-pool refill, check cost delta next billing day.
devon: TL;DR: consolidation can recover ~12% unit cost, but risk is egress policer + cache miss. Canary, limiter, rotate targets. :thumbsup:
ashley: Sounds good. I'll post status in ~2h.
_note: This document is a synthetic Slack thread, formatted per agents.md rules.
